threads.body: I'm aware that the progress bar uses the fill color associated with required artifacts, but the color is very close to red. Red is associated with negativity or danger in western cultures (in China it is good luck). To me at first glance this 100% filled required bar looked like a very bad number. Could we use a neutral color (doesn't have to be black), with maybe the same legend color box? For the signals list, using the requirement level fill color should be fine, since the legend is just below: What do you think?

replies.body: updated to try and use some more neutral colors

threads.body:
`genai_expected_attribute_missing` puts its attribute under `context.missing_attribute`, not `attribute_key`, so these findings fall back to grouping by message. Two things follow from that, and both go against the doc comment on `model()`:

- They're grouped per span instead of per attribute. On crewai/openllmetry, 3 attributes missing on 4 spans become 12 groups, while `recommended_attribute_not_present` would collapse the same situation into one group per attribute with where-chips.
- They never fold into the coverage row. On agno/openinference, `gen_ai.response.id`, `server.address` and the others appear under "Expected, not emitted" and again under "Recommended attributes not emitted" (behind "Show all 21"), although the former says it lists only absences "that aren't already listed above".

If folding is intended:
```js
const attribute =
  finding.context?.attribute_key ?? finding.context?.missing_attribute ?? null;
```
If keeping them separate is deliberate, because the GenAI rule is operation-specific, the comment and the section note should say so instead. Longer term, emitting a normalized `attribute` per finding from `_aggregate.py` would save the view from tracking each rule's context keys.

The new "Instrumentations" nav entry lands here with no id, and the page is just the heading and a picker button. Could the no-id case show something useful, such as the list of targets or a short prompt? Also, `palette()` turns the label into "Choose a instrumentation…", so it may need an `an`.

This replaces the masthead `<h1>` and tagline, and no view renders an `<h1>`, so headings now start at the `<h2>` in each view. Could the brand text stay an `<h1>`, or each view's title become one? The tagline ("What instrumentations actually emit, measured through Weaver live-check…") also disappears from the UI. Was that intentional?

threads.body: nit: `#/target/` with a trailing slash doesn't match `^\/target(?:\/(.+))?$`, so it falls through to `ROUTES[0]` and shows the heatmap with "Signal parity" highlighted. `^\/target(?:\/(.*))?$` plus treating `""` as no id would handle it. `/signals/` behaves the same way already, so this is optional.

nit: `signalKey` and `compareUrl` duplicate `data.js`'s `signalKey` and the `/signals/${encodeURIComponent(…)}` path in `signals.js:132`. Now that `route.js` has `targetPath`/`targetHref`, a matching `signalPath`/`signalHref` there, plus exporting `signalKey` from `data.js`, would leave one place to change each format.

threads.body:
The neutral `--fill-neutral` on the tile bars (plus the level dot in the label) already fixes the summary bar reading as an alarm, so I don't think `--required` needs to change globally. On the signals list the level colors are fine, since the legend is right there.

The teal also makes the levels harder to tell apart:

| Pair | Before (red) | Now (teal) |
|---|---|---|
| required vs recommended (`#1d6fa5`), normal vision | ΔE 74 | ΔE 41 |
| required vs recommended, tritanopia (light) | ΔE ~100 | ΔE 7.4 (nearly identical) |
| required vs `--good` (`#1a7f5a`) | | ΔE ~18 |

`--good` colors the ✓ cells in the heatmap, right next to the level dots. Dark mode (`#2dd4bf` vs `#6fb6e0` / `#4fc294`) is similar.

~~Could we keep the previous red for `--required`~~, now that `--bad` carries the failure meaning separately? Or pick a hue that's clearly apart from both the blue and the green?

(ΔE is CIE76 in Lab, with Machado 2009 simulation for the color-vision cases.)

replies.body: Reverting to red has its own problem: under deuteranopia #b4295c vs --good comes out at ΔE ≈ 2, and those sit next to each other on the heatmap. I went with purple (#8b2fc9 / #c77dff). Its worst case across normal vision, protanopia, deuteranopia and tritanopia is ≈ 21–23, versus recommended and conditional.

Thanks for restoring the `<h1>`. The tagline ("What instrumentations actually emit, measured through Weaver live-check against the pinned registries.") is still gone, though. It was the only place the UI said what the site measures and how. Was dropping it intentional? If space in the masthead is the issue, it could live under the heading on the Signals view, or in the `title` of the brand link.
